newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says France commited to EMU on time.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says France commited to EMU on time.

text.p: New Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin told parliament on Thursday he was committed to achieving a single European currency on time in January 1999.
But he made no mention of meeting the economic criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU) and said the euro must go hand in hand with economic solidarity to create growth and jobs.

"The feebleness of growth is a problem facing the whole of Europe. There must therefore be a common response. In this perspective, we reaffirm our determination to achieve economic and monetary union at the deadline provided for by the treaty," Jospin said in his keynote policy speech.

"But you cannot share a currency without creating economic solidarity. Concerning the independence of a (European) central bank, it does not mean a political vacuum. That was the meaning of the proposals we made (at this week's European Union summit) in Amsterdam," he said.
Jospin said the summit's resolution on jobs and growth was only a start and France would push for a reinforcement of a social Europe.
At home, he pledged to create the conditions for more vigorous economic growth.
